prompt:
"""Volleyball event detection: the whole system, as code. This file is what evolves.

Seed version: Gemini 4 Argon watches every 30 s clip (5 fps, high resolution, thinking high) with
the prompt evolved by evo2; overlapping clips are merged in code. No reviewer, no checks.
Now: a Flash gate drops dead clips, Flash marks the rallies in live clips, and the Argon scout watches
only padded rally windows (full resolution); off-sheet shirt numbers are re-read from a zoomed cut."""
import tools

PROMPT = """This is a volleyball match. This clip begins at {start} seconds into the match and runs for {length} seconds.

List every serve, receive, set, dig, attack, kill and block you see. Follow these logging rules:
- Do not log routine sets during a rally; only log a set if it directly precedes a point-winning kill.
- Only log a block if it is a stuff block that directly ends the rally; do not log block jumps or soft block deflections where play continues.
- Never log both an attack and a kill for the same hit: if the spike wins the point, log it only as a kill; otherwise log it as an attack. Only log actual spikes/attack hits; never log soft free-ball passes or standing bumps sent over the net as attacks.
- Only log a dig when a defender successfully keeps an opponent's attack in play; never log a routine free-ball pass or a failed defensive touch or shank after a point-winning kill.

For each one give:
  t      - the time in absolute match seconds (clip start {start} + offset)
  type   - serve, receive, set, dig, attack, kill or block
  side   - "left" or "right" of the net
  number - the player's shirt number, or null
  error  - true if it was an error
  point  - true if it won the point"""

SIDE_TO_TEAM = {"left": "white", "right": "blue"}
MERGE_WINDOW = 1.2     # same type + team within this many seconds = one touch (a team never repeats a
                       # touch type that fast; overlapping clips time the same touch up to ~1.1 s apart)
SERVE_LAG = 0.6        # the model stamps the serve at the toss; the scout stamps the hand-ball contact


LIVE_PROMPT = """This is a 30 second clip of a volleyball match video (fixed side-on camera).
Is any point of the match being played at any moment in this clip: a serve, or a rally in progress
(also a rally that is already under way when the clip starts, or that begins near the end)?
Answer false only if the whole clip has no match play at all: players standing or walking between
points, a timeout, a set break, warm-up or practice drills (pepper, hitting lines), or an empty court.
Reply as JSON: {"live": true/false, "what": "<one sentence>"}"""
LIVE_SCHEMA = {"type": "OBJECT", "properties": {"live": {"type": "BOOLEAN"}, "what": {"type": "STRING"}},
               "required": ["live", "what"]}


def live_clips(match):
    """Some clips hold no match play (long breaks, set breaks, warm-up between sets). The Argon scout
    costs ~$0.105 a clip and on warm-up drills it invents whole fake rallies (attack/dig chains with no
    readable numbers). A Flash look at 2 fps, low media (~$0.002 a clip) says whether any play
    happens; only those clips go to the Argon scout. Unsure answers keep the clip."""
    def one(clip):
        try:
            ans = match.watch(clip[0], LIVE_PROMPT, fps=2, media="low", thinking="low", model=tools.FLASH,
                              schema=LIVE_SCHEMA)
        except tools.BudgetExceeded:
            raise
        except Exception:
            return True
        return (ans or {}).get("live") is not False
    return [c for c, live in zip(match.clips, match.map(one, match.clips)) if live]


RALLY_PROMPT = """This is a 30 second clip of a volleyball match video (fixed side-on camera). The clip
begins at {start} seconds into the match. List every rally that is in play at any moment in this clip:
from the serve (the server's toss) until the ball is dead (lands, goes out, or the referee stops play).
Include a rally already under way when the clip starts (start = {start}) and one still going when the
clip ends (end = {end}). Times are absolute match seconds (clip start {start} + offset).
Do not list warm-up or practice hitting, or players standing or walking between points.
Reply as JSON: {{"rallies": [{{"start": <seconds>, "end": <seconds>}}]}}"""
RALLY_SCHEMA = {"type": "OBJECT", "properties": {"rallies": {"type": "ARRAY", "items": {"type": "OBJECT",
                "properties": {"start": {"type": "NUMBER"}, "end": {"type": "NUMBER"}},
                "required": ["start", "end"]}}}, "required": ["rallies"]}
PRE, POST = 3.0, 4.0     # padding around a Flash rally span (Flash times at 2 fps are ~1-2 s loose)
JOIN = 4.0               # spans closer than this are watched as one window
MAX_WIN, OVERLAP = 20.0, 6.0   # watch_range limit; long rallies are split with this much overlap
FOLLOW_GAP = 4.0         # a window whose last touch is this close to its end and does not end the
FOLLOW_LEN = 14.0        # rally gets a follow-on window of this length (at most FOLLOW_ROUNDS times)
FOLLOW_ROUNDS = 2


def rally_spans(match, clips):
    """Where the rallies are. Flash at 2 fps, low media (~$0.003 a clip) marks each live clip's
    rallies; a failed answer keeps the whole clip."""
    def one(clip):
        name, start, length = clip
        try:
            ans = match.watch(name, RALLY_PROMPT.format(start=f"{start:.2f}", end=f"{start + length:.2f}"),
                              fps=2, media="low", thinking="low", model=tools.FLASH, schema=RALLY_SCHEMA)
            spans = [(float(r["start"]), float(r["end"])) for r in (ans or {}).get("rallies", [])]
        except tools.BudgetExceeded:
            raise
        except Exception:
            return [(start, start + length)]
        return [(max(a, start), min(b, start + length)) for a, b in spans
                if b >= a and b > start - 1 and a < start + length + 1]
    return [s for spans in match.map(one, clips) for s in spans]


def windows(spans, lo, hi):
    """Padded, joined rally spans cut into watch_range windows of at most MAX_WIN seconds."""
    out = []
    for a, b in sorted((max(lo, a - PRE), min(hi, b + POST)) for a, b in spans):
        if out and a - out[-1][1] < JOIN:
            out[-1][1] = max(out[-1][1], b)
        else:
            out.append([a, b])
    wins = []
    for a, b in out:
        if b - a < 8.0:      # a lone serve still needs the toss and the first touch in view
            a, b = a - (8.0 - (b - a)) / 2, b + (8.0 - (b - a)) / 2
        n = max(1, -int(-(b - a - OVERLAP) // (MAX_WIN - OVERLAP)))
        length = min(MAX_WIN, b - a) if n == 1 else MAX_WIN
        step = 0.0 if n == 1 else (b - a - MAX_WIN) / (n - 1)
        wins += [(round(a + i * step, 2), round(a + i * step + length, 2)) for i in range(n)]
    return wins


def ends_rally(e):
    return e.get("type") in ("kill", "block") or e.get("point") or e.get("error")


def scout(match):
    """The Argon scout (same prompt, 5 fps, high media, thinking high) watches only the rally windows
    instead of every whole 30 s clip: about 60% of live-clip seconds are dead time or the 8 s overlap
    seen twice. Frames are full resolution (no downscale) so shirt numbers stay readable."""
    lo, hi = match.window
    wins = windows(rally_spans(match, live_clips(match)), lo - PRE, hi + POST)

    def one(w):
        t0, t1 = w
        prompt = PROMPT.replace("{start}", f"{t0:.2f}").replace("{length}", f"{t1 - t0:g}")
        try:
            answer = match.watch_range(t0, t1, prompt, fps=5, width=FRAME_W, model=tools.ARGON,
                                       thinking="high", schema=tools.EVENTS, media="high")
        except tools.BudgetExceeded:
            raise
        except Exception:
            return []
        return [dict(e, team=SIDE_TO_TEAM.get(e.get("side")), clip_start=t0, clip_len=t1 - t0)
                for e in (answer or {}).get("events", []) if t0 - 1.0 <= e.get("t", -1e9) <= t1 + 1.0]

    events, todo = [], wins
    for rnd in range(FOLLOW_ROUNDS + 1):
        results = match.map(one, todo)
        events += [e for evs in results for e in evs]
        if rnd == FOLLOW_ROUNDS:
            break
        nxt = []
        for (t0, t1), evs in zip(todo, results):
            last = max(evs, key=lambda e: e["t"], default=None)
            if last and not ends_rally(last) and t1 - last["t"] < FOLLOW_GAP and t1 < hi \
                    and not any(t1 < b and a < t1 + 1.0 for a, b in wins if (a, b) != (t0, t1)):
                nxt.append((round(t1 - OVERLAP, 2), round(t1 - OVERLAP + FOLLOW_LEN, 2)))
        wins += nxt
        todo = nxt
        if not todo:
            break
    return events


def merge(events):
    """Overlapping clips see the same touch twice: keep the copy furthest from its clip's edge."""
    def margin(e):
        off = e["t"] - e["clip_start"]
        return min(off, e["clip_len"] - off)
    out = []
    for e in sorted(events, key=lambda x: x["t"]):
        prior = next((o for o in reversed(out) if e["t"] - o["t"] <= MERGE_WINDOW and o["type"] == e["type"]
                      and o["team"] == e["team"]), None)
        if prior is None:
            out.append(e)
        elif margin(e) > margin(prior):
            out[out.index(prior)] = e
    return out


def roster(sheet):
    """Regular shirt numbers per team from the team sheet: the list before the first ';' on each
    side's line ('also seen once' numbers are unreliable and left out)."""
    out = {}
    for line in sheet.splitlines():
        for team in ("white", "blue"):
            if f"({team})" in line and ":" in line:
                main = line.split(":", 1)[1].split(";")[0]
                nums = ["".join(c for c in tok if c.isdigit()) for tok in main.split(",")]
                out[team] = [n for n in nums if n]
    return out


NUMBER_PROMPT = """This is a side-on view of one half of a volleyball court ({side} side of the net, the {team} team).
About {at:.1f} seconds into this clip a {team} player makes a {type} (one touch of the ball).
Find that touch and read the shirt number of the player who touches the ball. Look at every frame
where the player's front or back is visible; the number is printed on the shirt.
The {team} team's shirt numbers are: {numbers}. Answer with one of these, or null if the number
cannot be read in any frame. Do not guess from position or role.
Reply as JSON: {{"number": "<number or null>", "seen": "<what you saw, brief>"}}"""
FRAME_W, FRAME_H = 16 * 120, 9 * 120   # the raw clips are 1920x1080
HALF_W = FRAME_W // 2 + 160         # one half of the court plus the net zone
CROP = {"white": (0, 0, HALF_W, FRAME_H), "blue": (FRAME_W - HALF_W, 0, HALF_W, FRAME_H)}  # white left, blue right
BEFORE, AFTER = 1.0, 1.5


def fix_numbers(match, events):
    """The clip scout reads shirt numbers from the whole 1920-wide frame and often reports a number
    that is not on either team sheet (or none). Re-read those touches from a 2.5 s cut of that
    team's half of the court, choosing from the team's sheet; keep the old number otherwise."""
    teams = roster(match.team_sheet)
    todo = [e for e in events if e["team"] in teams and teams[e["team"]]
            and str(e.get("number") or "") not in teams[e["team"]]]

    def one(e):
        side = "left" if e["team"] == "white" else "right"
        prompt = NUMBER_PROMPT.format(side=side, team=e["team"], at=BEFORE, type=e["type"],
                                      numbers=", ".join(teams[e["team"]]))
        ans = match.watch_range(e["t"] - BEFORE, e["t"] + AFTER, prompt, fps=10, width=HALF_W,
                                crop=CROP[e["team"]], model=tools.ARGON, thinking="medium",
                                schema={"type": "OBJECT", "properties": {"number": {"type": "STRING", "nullable": True},
                                        "seen": {"type": "STRING"}}, "required": ["number", "seen"]})
        n = "".join(c for c in str((ans or {}).get("number") or "") if c.isdigit())
        return n if n in teams[e["team"]] else None

    for e, n in zip(todo, match.map(one, todo)):
        if n:
            e["number"] = n
    return events


def analyse(match):
    events = fix_numbers(match, merge(scout(match)))
    return [{"t": e["t"] + (SERVE_LAG if e["type"] == "serve" else 0.0), "type": e["type"], "team": e["team"], "number": e.get("number")} for e in events]

conjecture: Almost all of the cost ($14.4 of $16.03) is the Argon scout's video input: 150 high-media frames per 30 s clip, and it scales with seconds watched. Inside the live clips, about 55-60% of the seconds are dead time between points or the 8 s overlap that is watched twice. Rallies come every ~25 s and the clip stride is 22 s, so dropping whole clips cannot save more than ~2 clips per set (I checked a greedy cover of set 1's rallies: 48 of ~50 live clips are still needed). The only way to a large saving is to watch just the rallies. gen_02/cand_1 tried rally windows and lost on shirt numbers (0.68 -> 0.51) and on misses. This version differs: frames are cut at full 1920 width (no downscale to 1280); the existing dead-clip gate stays as is; Flash only marks rally spans inside live clips; padding is generous (3 s before, 4 s after, windows of at least 8 s); and the off-sheet number re-read (fix_numbers) now runs after the scout to catch number errors.

Full sets: cost about $9.5-11 per match (vs $16.03); for a fitness gain this saves 0.005-0.0065. Accuracy: the scout's answers are all new, so I expect noise. Set 1 OVERALL about 0.85-0.87 and set 2 about 0.85-0.87. Fitness about 0.848-0.858. It is kept only if accuracy holds within about 0.001 and set 2 does not drop. The main risks are missed touches where Flash cuts a rally short, and shirt numbers in the re-encoded cuts.

checks:
agent worked 12.0 min, 26 steps: I've changed `system.py` so the expensive Argon model watches only the rallies instead of every whole 30 s clip. It passes the harness check and `smoke.py` runs cleanly, but the real test is the harness run on sets 1 and 2, which hasn't happened yet.

**Why this change:** About $14.4 of the $16.03 per match is Argon reading video frames, and that cost grows with the seconds it watches. Simply skipping more clips can't save much. Rallies come about every 25 s and a new clip starts every 22 s, so nearly every clip holds part of a rally. Working by hand through set 1's rallies, about 48 of roughly 50 live clips are still needed. The only big saving is to skip the dead time between points and the 8 s each pair of neighbouring clips share.

**What changed:**
- **Dead-clip check:** the existing cheap check that drops clips with no play is unchanged.
- **Finding rallies:** a new cheap Flash call (about $0.003 a clip) gives the start and end time of each rally in every live clip. If that call fails, the whole clip is kept.
- **Building windows:** each rally gets 3 s added before and 4 s after, and nearby rallies are joined. Every window is at least 8 s, and long rallies are split into 20 s pieces that overlap by at least 6 s.
- **Watching:** Argon watches each window with the same prompt and settings as before (5 fps, high resolution, thinking high), at full 1920 width. If a window's last touch is near its end and doesn't end the point, a 14 s follow-on window is added, at most twice
